gloss: Points earned for verified strikes and spent on Brave1 Market. The programme gamifies real combat.
term: Ye-baly / e-points / Army of Drones Bonus

gloss: Uncrewed aerial vehicle.
ISDM truck-mounted rocket minelayer that scatters mines 5–15 km away.
Operational-strategic group of troops (e.g. Khortytsia).
Air defence.
Electronic warfare (jamming), and radio-electronic reconnaissance (SIGINT and direction finding).
Leaving a unit without authorisation, i.e. AWOL (Criminal Code Art. 407). Desertion is Art. 408.
The territorial recruitment centre (draft office), and slang for forcible street mobilisation into vans.
Army aviation, the Ukrainian helicopter branch. It is now also an anti-Shahed force.
Artillery. *Nasha arta* means "our guns".

"Cotton". Ironic slang for explosions on Russian-held targets. It mocks the Russian euphemism *khlopok* (хлопок), which means both "pop/bang" and "cotton". The game's name, *bavovniatko*, comes from this word.
"Roadlessness", the mud season. Russian *rasputitsa*.
Dugout or bunker with overhead cover.
The registry of verified Starlink terminals, created 2 Feb 2026 and enforced from 5 Feb. Unregistered (mostly Russian) terminals stopped working in Ukraine.
Evacuation, usually casualty evacuation.
DeepState status: blue for about two weeks after recapture, then green. The internal key is `dismissed`.
"Product", a Russian industrial designation, as in Izdeliye-53 (a Lancet successor) or Izdeliye 305 (LMUR).
"Guided aerial bomb": Ukrainian shorthand for any Russian glide bomb.
Ukraine's one-year voluntary contract for men below mobilisation age.
Kill zone: the drone-saturated belt where anything that moves gets struck. It is measured by strike density rather than the maximum range of a drone. About 10–15 km deep in 2025 and 15–30 km by 2026.
Forestry district: a named, managed forest block, such as the Serebrianske lisnytstvo.
Shelterbelt or treeline: a planted windbreak strip between fields. Russian *lesopolosa*.
Any small reconnaissance quadcopter, from the DJI Mavic.
Decoy or mock-up, such as a fake HIMARS.
Shahed/Geran drones, named for the moped-like sound of their engines.
Ground robotic system, i.e. a UGV.
DeepState's arrow icon for Russian offensive axes.
The "zero line", the forward-most occupied positions. *Na nuli* means "at the zero".
Fibre-optic FPV drone, steered through an unspooling cable and immune to radio jamming.
Wild Hornets' interceptor drone, and the generic word for an interceptor.
A position, the basic unit of Ukrainian defence, often held by 2–3 soldiers.
Soldiers' word for a treeline.
The fortress belt: Sloviansk–Kramatorsk–Druzhkivka–Kostiantynivka.
"Arrival" and "departure": an incoming impact, and an outgoing launch or sortie.
"Little birds" / "birds": drones. The source of the unit name "Magyar's Birds".
Infantry. Troops use it for the scarce trench infantry that everything depends on.
Rotation of troops on and off positions.
A drop: a munition or supply bundle released from a drone.
"Status unclear". Since 2026 it means areas of Russian infiltration with intermixed positions, not simple no-man's-land.
Grey zone: the contested ground between the lines. By 2025–26 it is often used as a synonym for the kill zone.
A conical spoil heap from a coal mine.
Air-raid alert.
"Turtle": a Russian vehicle fully boxed in against drones.
Shaheds, used generically for Geran one-way attack drones.
Assault soldier(s). Also used for the new assault regiments and the Assault Forces.
The NATO and US military symbology standards, and the code string that fully specifies a symbol.
Active protection system: radar-cued launchers that fire at incoming munitions or drones. An Arena-M tank took 15–20 FPVs to kill.
Russian messenger-style command-post software, reported as a Delta analogue.
Text or graphic fields around an APP-6 frame, and the unit-size marker drawn above it.
Cheap detectors can intercept and view analogue FPV video. Digital video can only be sensed as a signal, not viewed.
ISW's evidence tiers (backed by open-source evidence vs asserted by a party), and its layer, added in December 2025, for areas where Russian small groups operate without assessed control.
MoD AI platform that detects targets in drone and camera video.
Battlefield air interdiction: ISW's term for Russia's drone campaign against Ukrainian supply routes and vehicles in the near rear.
Battalion tactical group, the 2022 unit of action. Largely replaced by regiments and divisions by 2023.
The folk witch. Russian soldiers' name for Ukrainian heavy night bomber drones, which Ukrainians adopted. Russia's own copies carry the same nickname.
Ukrainian domestic 155 mm wheeled self-propelled howitzer.
The government defence-tech cluster, and its marketplace.
Command post exercise: staff training driven by a simulation.
Controlled reception pattern antenna: a multi-element anti-jam GNSS antenna (the Russian one is Kometa-M).
Ukrainian VR air-defence simulators, codified by the MoD in 2025.
BlueBird's detector for drone video signals.
ISW's usage: a counterattack is tactical, while a counteroffensive is operational-level, like Kharkiv or Kherson in 2022. Ukrainian officials avoided the word "counteroffensive" in Feb 2026.
A surface model that includes trees and buildings (e.g. Copernicus DEM), versus a bare-earth terrain model.
Air Assault Forces, the core of the 2026 Oleksandrivka offensive.
Ukraine's cloud-based situational-awareness and battle-management system. It also verifies e-point claims.
Delta modules for the live map and for assigning strike tasks.
Neither side sees the other's forces except through reports.
A multirotor that drops munitions instead of diving in.
Any detectable emission invites direction finding and a strike.
Russian general-purpose high-explosive bombs, numbered by weight in kg.
Forward arming and refuelling point; integrated air defence system; combat air patrol; releasing a weapon from outside the enemy's air-defence envelope.
First-person-view kamikaze quadcopter.
Planting a flag in a contested settlement for a photo, to fake a capture.
US programme that gave Ukraine access to commercial Maxar satellite imagery. Suspended for about a week in March 2025.
Ukrainian fire-allocation software, the "Uber for artillery".
Drowning out or faking satellite navigation signals. INS (inertial navigation) is the fallback, and it drifts over time.
Establishing where footage was shot by matching it to maps or satellite imagery.
Russian volunteer-built drone-to-fires software ("eye/thunderstorm"), and the Russian MoD's tactical situational-awareness complex.
When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring what matters. Relevant to e-points.
US wheeled rocket launcher, its guided 227 mm rocket, and its tactical ballistic missile.
Defence Intelligence of Ukraine.
Ukrainian ballistic missile programme.
Intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance.
Russian command-staff military games.
Heavy multirotor bomber drone, also used for resupply drops.
Ukrainian artillery C2 and mapping app, in use since 2014.
Line of contact.
Russian light multipurpose guided missile for Ka-52M and Mi-28NM helicopters, with about 15 km range.
Russian loitering munition, and a plywood fixed-wing strike drone.
The Drone Line project, which aims for a 10–15 km drone-dominated zone.
Ukrainian long-range strike drone.
A helicopter or jet climbs and releases unguided rockets on a ballistic arc, staying out of MANPADS range.
Broken Arrow's term for its planned one-way attack munitions.
A drone munition that searches before striking.
Assaulting along a shelterbelt's interior from its flank, versus crossing the open field into it (Parfonov).
Explosive line charges for breaching minefields.
An argument-based, adjudicated wargame, common in professional wargaming.
A radio network in which every node relays for the others, so the network survives losing nodes. The Chinese XK-F358 modem is used on Gerans, and Russian mesh chains control drones out to 150–175 km.

Ukrainian drone strikes at about 20–200 km depth against logistics, air defence and command posts. Logistics Lockdown is the MoD programme (27 May 2026) that funds middle-strike units through e-points, launched under Fedorov and continued under Khmara; the Kyiv Independent calls it "Logistical Lockdown".
Mobile fire groups: truck-mounted machine-gun or AA-gun teams that hunt Shaheds.
DeepState's monthly figure: the change in total Russian-occupied area. It hides gross gains and recaptures, which 07 §2.7 separates.
Order of battle.
A delayed batch of Ukrainian gains that DeepState publishes after an operation's security window has passed.
"Certain Areas of Donetsk/Luhansk Regions", occupied since 2014. Drawn separately from the post-2022 occupation.
On-screen display, the telemetry overlay on an FPV video feed.
The Patriot interceptor variant Ukraine relies on against ballistic missiles. Supply is squeezed by the 2026 Iran war.
Pseudo-random frequency hopping.
Crowdfunded ICEYE SAR satellite whose imagery goes to HUR.
Ukraine's nationwide GNSS-spoofing system. Lima is its main component.
EW operator.
ISW/CTP's daily *Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment*, and its control-of-terrain layer.
Received signal strength and link quality: measures of drone-link health.
"Real-time command action": Hell Of War's label for a command-drone view with drop-in direct control.
The Ukraine Defense Contact Group donor forum, and NATO's list of Ukraine's requirements (Europeans pay for US weapons, from Jul 2025).
Bureau 1440's Russian LEO satellite constellation, the planned Starlink substitute. It gives about 90 minutes of coverage a day as of 2026.
The Soviet and Russian sensor-to-shooter network concept. RUSI calls it the "Reconnaissance Fires Circuit".
Russia's elite Centre for Advanced Unmanned Technologies (about 5,000 personnel), used for deep drone interdiction and for hunting drone crews.
Unmanned Systems Forces, commanded from June 2025 by Robert "Madyar/Magyar" Brovdi.
Security Service of Ukraine. It ran Operation Spiderweb (*Pavutyna*, June 2025).
Suppression or destruction of enemy air defences; ground line of communication (a road or rail supply route).
Standard operating procedure. In Flashpoint Campaigns, the standing rules units follow between orders.
The linked sensors, C2 and fires that find and hit targets within minutes. Canadian games found it the hardest thing to break.
The Iranian-designed one-way attack drone and its Russian-built versions: piston engine, then jet (Geran-3 onward, with the Geran-5 air-launched from Jan 2026). Gerbera is a decoy.
Russian image-spoofing system aimed at drone video feeds.
MoD penal assault units of convicts. Z came with pardons (2023); V has none.
Russian reconnaissance, fire-control and communications data system.
The fortified belt in Zaporizhzhia built in 2022–23.
Temporarily occupied territories, the official Ukrainian term.
Machine-vision homing for the final few hundred metres after the radio link drops.
Territorial Defence Forces.
Russian gliding and correction kit that turns FAB dumb bombs into glide bombs.
SkyFall's heavy hexacopter bomber.
The "Great Meadow", the Dnipro floodplain once drowned by the Kakhovka reservoir and now regrowing.
Delta's video-analysis platform, and its module for planning and reporting drone missions.
Russian dish-array jammer that deafens Starlink satellites over about 20 km². It jams Ukraine's Starlink rather than replacing Russia's.
A simultaneous-turn system (as in Combat Mission): both sides plot, then execute together.
Monochrome thermal palettes, in which hotter objects appear white or black. Colour palettes include iron red (FLIR "ironbow"), arctic and rainbow.
Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Soviet-derived codes still in use: 200 = killed, 300 = wounded.
Russian milblogger term for inflated reports of advances sent up the chain of command.
Ukrainian official wording. "Restored control" covers grey-zone areas cleared of infiltrators rather than taken from full Russian control.
A broad, usually dry steppe gully, and a steeper, younger ravine.
Black-earth soil.
Summer cottage with a garden plot.
A Soviet apartment block of 4–5 storeys from 1956–1970s.
Soviet collective and state farms, the origin of the large-field grid.
"Barbecue grill": improvised cage armour against drones.
"Meat assaults": repeated attacks by expendable infantry.
To "zero" someone, i.e. execute them. The threat used against Russians who retreat.
Trench jammer, a jammer's protective "dome", and a backpack jammer. *Kupol* is also part of the name of the Russian Starlink jammer Volna Kupol Garant.
"Field-protective forest belts", the formal agronomic term for shelterbelts.
Industrial zone.
The "private sector": districts of single-family houses with gardens *(unverified)*.
Coal mine.
Anti-drone netting, and a net tunnel over a road.
Convicts: Wagner and Storm prisoner recruits.
Foliage season, or green cover *(unverified)*.
"Waiter": an ambush drone that lands near a road and waits for a target.
